months.headline: June 2025 saw a surge of TB research spanning neuroimaging, novel therapeutic targets, pediatric diagnostics, transplant risks, and promising regional eradication efforts.

points.text: A cohort study detailed the diverse MRI presentations of central nervous system tuberculosis, highlighting the complexity of neuro‑TB diagnosis.

Research identified M. tuberculosis adhesins as potential intervention points and introduced low‑complexity manual nucleic acid amplification tests for rapid pediatric pulmonary TB diagnosis, indicating advances in both treatment and detection.

Analyses of TB after renal transplantation and the immunogenicity of a Mycobacterium intracellulare isolate revealed heightened vulnerability in transplant recipients and the prospect of cross‑protective immunity for vaccine development.
Expert insights underscored tangible progress toward eradication, citing successful prevention strategies in Nariño, Colombia, as a model for broader TB‑free aspirations.

months.why_it_matters: These studies address critical gaps in TB detection, treatment, and prevention, especially for high‑risk groups, and signal tangible steps toward global eradication.

months.headline: July 2025 saw new strides in TB detection, treatment trials, and heightened public awareness across India, South Africa, China, and media.

points.text: A study in western Rajasthan, India, highlighted the need to bridge the diagnostic gap by implementing early detection of pulmonary TB among people living with HIV, aiming to reduce delayed diagnoses and improve outcomes.

Researchers in South Africa’s Limpopo province reported in‑vitro antioxidant and antimycobacterial activity of locally used medicinal plants, suggesting alternative options against drug‑resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

A safety and feasibility trial in Chinese children showed that a one‑month daily rifapentine plus isoniazid regimen achieved adequate plasma concentrations, offering a shorter preventive therapy for tuberculosis infection.
The TV series “Goodbye Deutschland” featured a woman dying of TB in Bali, sparking public shock and raising awareness of tuberculosis as a deadly infectious disease worldwide.

months.why_it_matters: These developments illustrate progress in early diagnosis, novel therapeutic approaches, and public perception of TB, all critical for controlling the disease, especially among vulnerable populations and in the face of rising drug resistance.

months.headline: August 2025 saw new insights into pediatric TB treatment adherence, promising therapeutic and diagnostic advances, and strategies to curb drug‑resistant TB

points.text: Research identified key predictors of early discontinuation of preventive therapy among children exposed to multidrug‑resistant TB, highlighting adherence challenges for WHO‑recommended levofloxacin regimens.

Two novel agents showed dual promise: netupitant demonstrated potent activity against persister MTB cells that drive relapse, and a solvatochromic naphthalimide‑benzothiazinone probe combined rapid detection with bacterial inhibition.
Long‑read amplicon sequencing was highlighted as a rapid, cost‑effective, user‑friendly diagnostic platform for TB and drug‑resistant TB, aligning with WHO’s call for better detection tools.

Fluoroquinolones, including levofloxacin, were emphasized to mitigate unfavorable outcomes and prevent acquired rifampicin resistance in isoniazid‑resistant TB, reinforcing updated treatment guidelines.

months.why_it_matters: These findings address critical gaps in TB control—improving child adherence, offering new therapeutic and diagnostic tools, and strengthening regimens against drug‑resistant strains—thereby supporting global efforts to reduce TB morbidity and mortality.

months.headline: September 2025 saw rising concerns over drug‑resistant TB and innovative AI‑driven bovine TB surveillance

points.text: Experts outlined the persistent hurdles in TB drug discovery, emphasizing the need for new therapeutic targets and better pipelines to combat the disease's high mortality and resistance potential.
A study documented the transmission of bedaquiline‑resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in KwaZulu‑Natal, South Africa, warning that resistance to this key drug could undermine modern DR‑TB regimens.
Researchers applied AI to field data, improving detection and prediction of bovine tuberculosis in Tunisian cattle, highlighting the zoonotic and economic stakes of TB beyond human patients.

months.why_it_matters: TB remains a leading global health threat; emerging drug resistance threatens treatment gains, while zoonotic TB in livestock poses both economic losses and a reservoir for human infection.

months.headline: Policy shifts, diagnostic advances, and vaccine safety studies mark October 2025 for tuberculosis

points.text: Indonesia adopted a COVID‑era integrated management model to accelerate its goal of eliminating tuberculosis by 2030, signaling a major policy shift in TB control.

Researchers demonstrated that whole‑lung CT radiomics combined with clinical features can differentiate multidrug‑resistant TB from drug‑sensitive TB, offering a new tool for early detection of resistant strains.

A nationwide Korean cohort study compared the safety of intradermal Danish‑1331 versus transcutaneous Tokyo‑172 BCG strains, finding comparable safety profiles and informing future vaccination strategies.

months.why_it_matters: These developments combine strategic policy action, improved diagnostic capability for drug‑resistant TB, and evidence‑based vaccine safety data, all crucial for accelerating global TB elimination efforts.

months.headline: Global TB diagnoses climb while India records a sharp incidence drop and new diagnostics emerge

points.text: India celebrated a 21% decline in TB incidence since 2015, a success highlighted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi after the release of the WHO Global TB Report 2025, demonstrating the impact of intensified national control efforts.

Molecular diagnostics are gaining traction, with experts in New York noting incremental progress toward case reduction, while a novel phage‑based qPCR assay has enabled accurate detection of mycobacterial co‑infections in cattle, improving bovine TB surveillance.
A case report of pulmonary TB in an immunocompromised patient raised questions about the interplay of HIV, COVID‑19, and TB, highlighting the heightened vulnerability of co‑infected individuals.

months.why_it_matters: The rise in global TB diagnoses signals ongoing public‑health challenges, while India's incidence drop shows that aggressive national strategies can work. Advances in diagnostics for both humans and livestock are critical for early detection and containment, especially among high‑risk, immunocompromised populations.

months.headline: December 2025 saw new TB diagnostics, innovative drug delivery research, and major US‑Nigeria/Kenya health deals to combat drug‑resistant TB

points.text: The FDA‑approved vital staining method was shown to effectively monitor drug‑resistant pulmonary TB patients on extended regimens, offering a simple early‑failure detection tool under the NTEP.
Researchers reported surface‑engineered ethambutol‑loaded nanoparticles that improve oral bioavailability and target delivery, addressing key limitations of current TB chemotherapy.

The United States signed multi‑billion‑dollar five‑year health agreements with Nigeria ($5.1 b) and Kenya ($2.5 b), explicitly targeting infectious diseases including TB, to strengthen health systems and expand treatment capacity.

months.why_it_matters: TB remains a leading global health threat, especially in its drug‑resistant forms; early detection, novel therapeutics, and substantial funding commitments are essential to sustain and accelerate progress against the disease.

months.headline: January 2026 saw new clinical case reports, a labor‑driven outbreak response, and advances in TB biology and diagnostics.

points.text: Case series highlighted the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of leprosy‑TB co‑infection and tuberculous mastitis, underscoring the complexity of extrapulmonary TB presentations.

The GMB union demanded the temporary closure of Amazon's Coventry warehouse after multiple TB cases were reported, while the company reported successful treatment of affected workers and no new infections.
Researchers at IISc and IMSC identified a key TB protein that shields the bacterium from foreign DNA, revealing a potential target for novel therapeutics.
A study evaluated the simple one‑step (SOS) stool method for TruNat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/XDR assays, showing promise for easier, child‑friendly TB diagnosis.

months.why_it_matters: These developments highlight ongoing clinical challenges, occupational health risks, and scientific progress that could shape TB control strategies, drug development, and pediatric testing.

months.headline: February 2026 saw new policy evaluations, cost‑saving treatment findings, and heightened public attention to TB outbreaks across India and Malaysia.

points.text: A qualitative study examined Tamil Nadu's differentiated TB care initiative (TN‑KET), launched in 2022 to streamline triage for severe TB and reduce deaths.
The Indian Council of Medical Research reported that shorter TB treatment regimens are both clinically effective and cost‑effective, suggesting a potential shift in national treatment protocols.
Malaysian lawmakers raised TB outbreaks as a key issue in a parliamentary session, indicating growing governmental concern alongside trade and labour topics.
In Johor, three school pupils recovered from TB while four remain under monitoring, and a separate kidnapping case involved a mother receiving TB treatment, highlighting the disease's social impact.

months.why_it_matters: These findings and political attention could accelerate adoption of shorter, cheaper treatment regimens and strengthen targeted care models, while the outbreaks and related social incidents underscore the need for robust public health responses.

months.headline: March 2026 saw heightened alarm over tuberculosis spread and under‑diagnosis, alongside promising new therapeutic breakthroughs.

points.text: The World Health Organization issued an urgent call for sustained collective action to end TB, warning it remains a major public‑health threat especially in the Eastern Mediterranean region.
Reports highlighted a hidden ‘white plague’ crisis in the UK and Europe, with health services failing to identify or treat roughly one‑in‑five TB cases.
A forensic case of disseminated TB with granulomatous pericarditis underscored the diagnostic challenges the disease poses in unexpected deaths.
Research unveiled novel treatments—a photothermal‑silver nanoparticle nanoplatform and the antibiotic Questiomycin A targeting fabD—offering new hope against intracellular and multidrug‑resistant TB.

months.why_it_matters: TB continues to threaten global health through rising drug resistance and under‑diagnosis, demanding coordinated policy action and innovative therapies to curb its spread.

months.headline: April 2026 saw AI-driven diagnostic breakthroughs in India, rising TB hotspots in North America, and a rare successful treatment of severe disseminated TB.

points.text: An artificial‑intelligence system in India achieved 92–100% accuracy interpreting TB line‑probe assay strips, offering a highly reliable tool for rapid diagnosis across multiple labs.

Regional TB burdens remained high, with Saskatchewan identified as one of Canada’s provinces with the highest rates and Texas reporting 1,279 cases in 2024, prompting local health officials to intensify control efforts.

A case of fulminant disseminated TB presenting as Landouzy sepsis was successfully managed with ECMO support and an individualized antituberculous regimen, highlighting the potential of advanced critical‑care strategies for rare, severe TB forms.

months.why_it_matters: Accurate AI diagnostics can accelerate case detection and treatment, while persistent high‑incidence pockets underscore ongoing public‑health challenges; the rare successful treatment demonstrates the importance of specialized care for severe TB manifestations.

months.headline: May 2026 saw new high‑dose rifampicin evidence, a rapid portable TB test, funding threats, and rising vaccine hesitancy in China.

points.text: A systematic review and meta‑analysis found that daily regimens with high‑dose rifampicin may be more efficacious and safe than standard doses, which sit at the lower end of the exposure‑response curve.

The Minidock MTB portable test delivers near‑point‑of‑care TB detection in minutes with about 86% sputum sensitivity, ~80% tongue‑swab sensitivity and >97% specificity, matching Xpert Ultra while enabling non‑invasive sampling.
The U.S. administration is seeking to redirect $2 billion from global health programs to cover costs associated with the closure of USAID, threatening funding for TB control initiatives.
In China, an increasing number of parents are refusing infant inoculations, including the tuberculosis BCG jab, intensifying a public‑health crisis as the government pushes to contain it.

months.why_it_matters: These developments affect TB treatment effectiveness, diagnostic speed, financial support for control programs, and vaccine coverage, all critical to global TB elimination goals.

data.arc: From mid‑2025 the field moved from a broad surge of research on neuro‑TB, novel targets and pediatric diagnostics toward more applied trials and public awareness campaigns, especially in high‑burden countries. By late 2025 the focus shifted to policy reforms and large‑scale vaccination safety studies, while India reported a notable decline in incidence. Early 2026 highlighted biological breakthroughs and cost‑effective treatment regimens, but also underscored persistent gaps: drug‑resistant transmission, under‑diagnosis in Europe, and emerging funding and vaccine‑hesitancy challenges. The coming months will test whether new AI‑driven diagnostics, high‑dose rifampicin strategies, and international financing can sustain momentum against a disease that remains a global public‑health threat.

turning_points.why: A surge of multidisciplinary TB research signaled a renewed scientific push across diagnostics, therapeutics, and eradication models.
Indonesia’s adoption of an integrated management model marked a major policy shift aimed at accelerating elimination by 2030.
India reported a 21% decline in TB incidence, demonstrating the impact of intensified national control efforts.
WHO’s urgent call highlighted a hidden crisis of under‑diagnosis and drug‑resistance, refocusing global attention on gaps in detection and treatment.
Funding redirection threats and rising BCG hesitancy in China introduced new systemic risks to TB control progress.
